messages:
ben: FYI started canary deploy `release/2026.03.15-22` to 5% ~ 02:12 UTC. small rollout but saw immediate spike on gen-latency.slo :frowning:
liam: saw that alert too, paging now?
sre-bot: Pager triggered for policy `gen-latency.slo > 1.5s p95` — 3 duplicate alerts in 60s.
ben: Yep, multiple p95 alerts. No obvious error traces in traces.prod for the canary tag. latency only.
jules: pinging infra — any kernel churn or network flaps in the cluster hosting canary?
ops-bot: Deploy job `canary/2026.03.15-22` reported: `k8s rollout succeeded` (3 pods ready).
liam: I can take first touch. oncall right now. Starting quick triage: check canary routing and rate.
liam: quick check: canary traffic routed by header `x-experiment: beta-scheduler` to pool gpu-pool-b.
liam: run `kubectl logs -l app=scheduler -c inference --since=5m | grep "latency"` -> getting lots of "kv-cache-miss" and long decode times.
ben: interesting — that suggests remote KV cache misses rather than model slowdown. canary's kernel selection might be switching quantized path?
jules: we don't have a dedicated dashboard for the canary pool (oops). all alerts are firing against global SLOs but no per-pool breakdown in console.
nana?: (typo)
liam: brb typo :)
nana?? (not used)
ben: big issue: we don't have a per-canary SLO dashboard in Redwood Console for gpu-pool-b. Alerting rules are global; noise is hiding whether production user traffic is impacted.
irene-cs: I have a customer on a live call asking about "sluggish responses" — not yet widespread but a couple of customers on downstream webhooks reported 3–5s delays.
liam: OK that confirms customer impact small but real. priority to stop rollout or flip feature flag. can we flip the scheduler experiment flag?
jules: flag exists: `feature.new_scheduler.enabled` targeted to canary cohort. We have a kill endpoint: POST /flags/feature.new_scheduler/targeting/rollback
liam: prepare rollback but want to double-check logs for hotpath. if we flip flag it should route traffic back to old scheduler quickly.
ben: I'll prepare the kill command.
ben: ```bash
# disable for canary cohort
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_OPS_TOKEN" \
  https://console.redwood.ai/api/flags/feature.new_scheduler/disable \
  -d '{"target":"cohort:beta-scheduler"}'
```
liam: good. also, until we flip, can we reduce canary % from 5% -> 0.5% to buy time?
jules: autoscaler will respect new routing but need to patch rollout config. I'll run a canary shrink now.
jules: `kubectl patch rollout canary-scheduler --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"trafficPercent":0.5}}'`
ops-bot: Action acknowledged: canary traffic adjusted to 0.5%.
liam: traffic drop confirmed by sampling: 5% -> ~0.6% in the last 30s. p95 dropped a bit but still above SLO.
ben: I'm going to flip the flag now to be safe. Will post when done.
ben: POST triggered — waiting for propagation.
ben: done. propagation log: `flag-change executed -> 2026-03-15T02:18:45Z`
ops-bot: Feature flag `feature.new_scheduler` updated: disabled for cohort `beta-scheduler` (request by ben).
liam: traffic is routing back to old scheduler nodes. p95 halfway back to normal within 45s.
liam: note: we're still getting a flood of the same alert duplicates. looks like alert dedupe misconfigured for canary bursts -> generating noise and obscuring signal.
jules: that's the observability gap: alert noise + no canary dashboard. I'll file a quick ticket to add canary-specific panels and per-pool SLOs.
ben: Filed ticket DEVOPS-4321: "canary: per-pool dashboards + alert dedupe" — assigning to eng-platform.
ben: Suggest follow-up: make alerting scope aware (ignore canary bursts under 1% route change unless sustained 2m) and add a `canary:true` tag on alerts.
liam: agreed. Also we need a runbook update: on deploy alerts, check `routing.pool` tag and `feature.flag` tag before paging global SLO owners. Right now the pager doesn't carry those fields.
jules: noted — I'll update runbook and create alert change PR.
irene-cs: any customer mitigation notes for CS? I can tell customers we've rolled back and are monitoring, ETA for root cause TBD.
ben: Tell them rollback done, latency returning, we'll follow up with RCA and if they saw errors to DM me with request ids.
liam: handing off to next oncall (ana) in 20m. leaving notes: rollout flipped, canary shrunk, alerts noisy due to dedupe gap, file DEVOPS-4321 created.
nana?? (typo again: meant ana)
ana: ack — I'm Ana, taking the handoff. I'll watch the next 30m and ensure SLO stabilizes and the follow-up ticket lands.
liam: thanks — also set a reminder to run the canary again after infra-side KV cache warmup patch lands.
ana: will do.
liam: closing the active page — mark as mitigated. please escalate if p95 climbs again. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident mitigated by liam — feature flag rollback executed; confidence: medium.
ben: quick retrospective notes: missing per-canary dashboards, alert dedupe config, pager payload lacks routing metadata. prioritize before next canary run.
ana: will own coordinating the dashboard work with eng-platform and SRE.
irene-cs: I'll send a note to affected customers summarizing rollback + next steps.
liam: thanks everyone. end of thread.
